newsitem.title: USA: Tighter US import policy on Canada barley - US group.
newsitem.headline: Tighter US import policy on Canada barley - US group.

text.p: The United States has warned Canada it would consider action if Canadian exports of barley to the United States grew to disruptive levels, U.S. National Barley Growers Association (NBGA) said Tuesday.

Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Friday in a letter to Canadian Trade Minister Art Eggleton that although 1995/96 imports of Canadian barley were lower, the U.S. administration remained concerned.

"Should imports of Canadian barley reach levels which threaten to disrupt the U.S. barley market, the United States would, of course, be prepared to consider taking appropriate action," Barshefsky's letter said.
Barshefsky discussed the barley situation with Eggleton at the Quadrilateral (Quad) trade ministers' meeting in Seattle last month.

In a statement, NBGA said U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman met barley producers in Montana last weekend and indicated the administration was prepared to act if there was an import surge, rather than waiting until imports reach 1993/94 levels.
It appeared to be a change from a Sept 17 joint statement by Glickman and Barshefsky in which they said they would consider action if imports of Canadian barley reached 1993/94 levels.
USDA officials could not immediately confirm that there had been a change in policy.
In its statement, NBGA said Glickman's most recent statement was encouraging but said a quantifiable, supply/demand monitoring mechanism was needed.
"Now, we need to develop some tools to define such terms as market disruption and import surges," NBGA President Craig Corbett said in the statement.
